title: Is the Occupancy Certificate (OC) available?
helpText: Verify that the competent authority has issued an Occupancy Certificate for the property/project.
whyItMatters: An Occupancy Certificate indicates that the completed development has received the required occupancy approval.
impact: Missing or unavailable occupancy approval can create significant legal, financing, resale, and possession-related risk.

title: Is the Sale Deed registered?
helpText: Verify that the property ownership document has been executed and registered with the appropriate authority.
whyItMatters: A registered Sale Deed is a key document establishing legal ownership of the property.
impact: An unregistered or incomplete ownership document can create ownership and transaction risks.

title: Is the property Khata available and correctly recorded?
helpText: Verify that the applicable Khata/e-Khata record exists and reflects the property correctly.
whyItMatters: A valid property record supports taxation, municipal administration, financing, and future transactions.
impact: Incorrect, incomplete, or unavailable Khata records can create administrative and transaction-related risk.

title: Is the Encumbrance Certificate (EC) available?
helpText: Verify the availability of an Encumbrance Certificate covering the relevant property period.
whyItMatters: An EC provides information about registered transactions or encumbrances reflected in the relevant records.
impact: Missing or incomplete EC documentation can make ownership due diligence less complete.

title: Are there no significant structural cracks?
helpText: Inspect visible walls, slabs, beams, columns, balconies, and other relevant structural areas for significant cracks.
whyItMatters: Significant cracks may indicate construction defects, movement, water ingress, or other issues requiring professional assessment.
impact: Unresolved significant cracks can result in safety concerns, property damage, and future repair costs.
requiredEvidence: Structural engineer report for suspected structural cracks

title: Is the property free from significant water leakage?
helpText: Check ceilings, walls, bathrooms, balconies, utility areas, parking areas, and other relevant locations for water leakage.
whyItMatters: Water leakage can damage finishes, electrical systems, structures, and personal property.
impact: Persistent leakage can result in deterioration, mould, repair costs, and disputes over responsibility.

title: Is the property free from significant dampness?
helpText: Inspect walls, ceilings, corners, bathrooms, balconies, and other areas for persistent dampness or moisture marks.
whyItMatters: Dampness may indicate water ingress, plumbing problems, waterproofing failure, or ventilation issues.
impact: Persistent dampness can deteriorate finishes and contribute to recurring maintenance problems.

title: Is the flooring quality satisfactory?
helpText: Check flooring for cracks, hollow tiles, uneven surfaces, damaged tiles, or significant workmanship defects.
whyItMatters: Flooring defects can affect usability, safety, appearance, and long-term maintenance.
impact: Unresolved flooring defects can lead to replacement costs and recurring maintenance issues.

title: Is the paint and surface finish quality satisfactory?
helpText: Check internal and external painted surfaces for peeling, patchiness, cracks, stains, or poor workmanship.
whyItMatters: Paint and surface finishes provide protection as well as contributing to property condition and appearance.
impact: Poor finishes can indicate workmanship issues and may require premature repainting or repair.

title: Is waterproofing satisfactory in critical areas?
helpText: Verify waterproofing performance in bathrooms, balconies, terraces, wet areas, basements, and other relevant locations.
whyItMatters: Effective waterproofing protects the building from water ingress and associated deterioration.
impact: Waterproofing failures can cause leakage, dampness, structural deterioration, and expensive repairs.

title: Is the BESCOM electricity connection and metering operational?
helpText: Verify electricity connection, individual/common metering, and relevant BESCOM documentation where applicable.
whyItMatters: Reliable electricity supply and appropriate metering are essential for normal property operation.
impact: Incomplete electrical infrastructure or documentation can create operational and financial risk.

title: Is the BWSSB water and sewerage connection operational?
helpText: Verify applicable water and sewerage connections, approvals, billing arrangements, and supporting records.
whyItMatters: Reliable water and sewerage infrastructure is fundamental to property habitability and long-term operation.
impact: Incomplete or unavailable water and sewerage arrangements can result in operational, financial, and compliance risks.

title: Is the Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) operational and maintained?
helpText: Verify that the STP is operational, maintained, and supported by relevant operating or maintenance records.
whyItMatters: Proper sewage treatment is important for environmental compliance and community infrastructure.
impact: Poorly maintained or non-operational STP infrastructure can create environmental, regulatory, and maintenance risks.

title: Is the Water Treatment Plant (WTP) operational where applicable?
helpText: Verify WTP operation, maintenance, and relevant water-quality records where a WTP forms part of the property infrastructure.
whyItMatters: Appropriate water treatment infrastructure supports reliable and suitable water availability.
impact: Non-operational or poorly maintained treatment infrastructure can affect water quality and availability.

title: Is DG backup operational where applicable?
helpText: Verify diesel generator backup availability, operational status, maintenance, and relevant records where applicable.
whyItMatters: Backup power can support critical common-area infrastructure during electricity interruptions.
impact: Non-operational backup power may affect lifts, pumps, security systems, and other common services during outages.

title: Are the lifts operational and appropriately maintained?
helpText: Verify lift operation, maintenance arrangements, inspection records, and applicable certifications.
whyItMatters: Lift reliability and maintenance are important for accessibility, convenience, and resident safety.
impact: Poorly maintained lifts can result in service interruptions and safety concerns.

title: Is adequate water availability maintained?
helpText: Assess whether the property has reliable water availability through its applicable water sources and storage systems.
whyItMatters: Reliable water availability is essential for everyday residential use and community operations.
impact: Frequent water shortages can create significant operational and resident-management challenges.

title: Is the Fire NOC available and valid where applicable?
helpText: Verify the applicable Fire Department approval/NOC and supporting compliance records.
whyItMatters: Fire-safety approvals and compliance arrangements are important for resident safety and statutory requirements.
impact: Missing or unclear fire approvals can create significant safety and compliance risk.

title: Are emergency exits accessible and clearly identified?
helpText: Check that designated emergency exits are accessible, unobstructed, and appropriately identified.
whyItMatters: Accessible emergency exits support safe evacuation during fires and other emergencies.
impact: Blocked, unclear, or inaccessible exits can increase evacuation risk.

title: Is the fire-fighting system operational and maintained?
helpText: Verify fire pumps, hydrants, alarms, extinguishers, sprinklers, and other applicable fire-fighting systems.
whyItMatters: Operational fire-fighting systems are critical to responding to fire emergencies.
impact: Non-operational or poorly maintained fire systems can materially increase safety risk.

title: Is CCTV coverage operational in relevant common areas?
helpText: Verify that installed CCTV systems cover relevant common areas and are operational where applicable.
whyItMatters: CCTV can support incident investigation, monitoring, and community security processes.
impact: Non-operational or inadequate CCTV coverage can reduce monitoring capability in common areas.

title: Is an adequate security arrangement in place?
helpText: Assess whether the property has documented security arrangements appropriate to the community and property type.
whyItMatters: Defined security procedures can help manage access, incidents, visitors, and common-area safety.
impact: Weak or undocumented security arrangements may increase operational and resident-safety risks.

title: Is lightning protection installed and maintained where applicable?
helpText: Verify the presence and maintenance of applicable lightning protection systems.
whyItMatters: Lightning protection can help reduce risks associated with lightning strikes to buildings and infrastructure.
impact: Missing or poorly maintained lightning protection may increase exposure to lightning-related damage and safety risks.

title: Has the apartment association been formally formed?
helpText: Verify whether the apartment owners association or resident welfare association has been formally established.
whyItMatters: A formally established association is important for managing common areas, maintenance, contracts, utilities, and community responsibilities.
impact: An unformed association can create gaps in maintenance governance and ownership of common responsibilities.

title: Is the corpus fund established and documented?
helpText: Check whether a corpus or sinking fund has been collected and whether the amount and purpose are documented.
whyItMatters: A corpus fund provides financial preparedness for major repairs, replacements, and long-term common-area maintenance.
impact: Absence of a documented corpus fund may increase the risk of unexpected maintenance contributions.

title: Are required Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMCs) in place?
helpText: Verify whether critical systems and equipment have active maintenance contracts where applicable.
whyItMatters: AMCs help ensure critical equipment and infrastructure receive scheduled maintenance and servicing.
impact: Missing or expired AMCs can increase equipment downtime, maintenance risk, and unexpected repair costs.

title: Are key community vendor contracts documented?
helpText: Check whether contracts with important service providers are documented and currently valid.
whyItMatters: Clear vendor contracts establish service expectations, responsibilities, pricing, duration, and escalation mechanisms.
impact: Undocumented vendor arrangements can create service continuity, accountability, and cost-management risks.

title: Is there a documented complaint resolution process?
helpText: Verify whether residents have a defined process for registering, tracking, escalating, and closing complaints.
whyItMatters: A structured complaint process improves accountability and helps ensure resident issues are tracked through resolution.
impact: Without a documented process, complaints may be missed, delayed, or difficult to escalate and close.

title: Are the property tax records available and up to date?
helpText: Verify that the applicable property tax records are available and that the property tax status can be confirmed.
whyItMatters: Property tax records provide supporting evidence of municipal tax compliance and help maintain an organized property record.
impact: Missing or unclear property tax records can create documentation and administrative gaps.
requiredEvidence: Property tax assessment details where applicable

title: Are the BESCOM electricity documents available?
helpText: Verify that relevant electricity connection, metering, billing, and supporting BESCOM records are available.
whyItMatters: Maintaining electricity documentation helps establish the status of the connection and supports future service or ownership-related requirements.
impact: Missing electricity documentation can make utility verification and future issue resolution more difficult.
requiredEvidence: Relevant correspondence or approvals where applicable

title: Are the BWSSB water and sewerage documents available?
helpText: Verify that relevant BWSSB connection, billing, approval, demand, and payment records are available where applicable.
whyItMatters: Water and sewerage documentation supports verification of the property infrastructure and ongoing utility arrangements.
impact: Missing or incomplete BWSSB records can create utility verification and administrative gaps.
requiredEvidence: Relevant approvals or correspondence where applicable

title: Are property and equipment warranty documents available?
helpText: Verify that applicable builder, equipment, appliance, waterproofing, and system warranty documents are retained.
whyItMatters: Warranty records help owners identify coverage periods, responsible parties, and available remedies when defects or failures occur.
impact: Missing warranty documentation can make it harder to establish coverage and pursue eligible rectification or service.

title: Are maintenance manuals and relevant property records available?
helpText: Verify that applicable operation manuals, maintenance manuals, asset records, handover documents, and service information are retained.
whyItMatters: Maintenance manuals and property records help owners and associations operate, maintain, and service building systems correctly.
impact: Missing manuals and handover records can increase maintenance dependency, delay troubleshooting, and reduce continuity of property management.
